data.title: Exclusive-US should not certify Chinese aircraft, restrict investments in China's aerospace sector, lawmakers say
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government should refuse to certify Chinese-made airplanes and pull taxpayer contracts from American defense contractors including Airbus if they do not halt investments in China's aerospace industrial base, a congressional report seen by Reuters said.

The House Select Committee on China in a report said Washington should toughen export controls and restrict investments in China's aerospace sector.

"The broader system allowed commercial aerospace engagement that could strengthen firms connected to the PRC's military industrial base without triggering the safeguards designed to protect sensitive technology," the report said following a year-long investigation.

Airbus did not immediately comment.

The report said the Federal Aviation Administration should not allow Chinese-manufactured aircraft to fly in the United States, noting that China has never released its report into the 2022 crash of a China Eastern Airlines Boeing aircraft and citing subsidies that China has given to state-owned Chinese airplane maker COMAC and AVIC. 

The Treasury Department should restrict outbound investment into China's aerospace sector and urge allies to follow suit and subject the purchase of US aerospace companies by French firms to heightened scrutiny until they unwind ties to China's "Civil-Military Ecosystem."

The report said through joint ventures, co-development agreements, and other commercial relationships "American and other Western companies transferred technology, know-how, and industrial capacity" on aerospace that ultimately benefited the Chinese military.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama )

data.title: Shufti Launches Glocal Trust OS, Connecting Business-Wide Information with User Risk Signals for Context-Aware Decisions

LONDON, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shufti, a Glocal identity verification, AML, and fraud prevention provider, has announced the launch of its Glocal Trust OS, an operating system that brings user lifecycle solutions together with businesses’ existing technology infrastructure in a unified environment, combining global capabilities adapted to local regulatory and operational requirements.

Risk assessments often depend on information scattered across internal applications, departmental systems, and third-party sources. Some records and critical knowledge may also be accessible only through specific teams or specialists, requiring additional requests and coordination before a decision can be made. This fragmentation limits visibility, delays investigations, and can leave relevant information out of risk assessments.

Glocal Trust OS addresses these gaps by connecting user lifecycle controls with existing business applications and external risk sources. Its architecture allows businesses to bring supported third-party applications, including email, Slack, and custom internal systems, into the same operating environment as Shufti's own solutions, without replacing their established technology.

At its core is a built-in intelligence layer called the Brain, which combines user identity information, verification history, activity, and risk signals with relevant information from connected business sources. This creates a single user view, with identity and risk context carried forward from onboarding through subsequent logins, payouts, and signatures.

How Does the Built-In Brain Bring Context to Risk Decisions?

The Brain uses this connected information to help businesses assess new activity against previous user interactions and available risk indicators, rather than relying on isolated checks.

A transaction may not trigger conventional monitoring rules but could still warrant further review when considered alongside recent account activity, earlier identity verification findings, or relevant third-party risk alerts. The Brain presents these related findings in context, helping reviewers identify concerns that might otherwise be overlooked.

The intelligence layer also supports natural-language interaction with connected information sources. Authorised teams can query relevant business and user information without manually searching different applications or depending on individual specialists to provide the necessary records. This gives compliance, risk, and operational teams more direct access to information needed for their assessments.

One Operating System for the Entire User Lifecycle

Glocal Trust OS unifies identity verification, AML, and fraud prevention across the user lifecycle, from initial onboarding and ongoing risk monitoring to securing critical actions through authentication and assurance, across three connected stages:

  • Onboard: Identity verification, KYC, KYB, and AML screening to establish user identity and assess initial risk.
  • Monitor: Fraud prevention, AML screening, and transaction monitoring to detect suspicious activity and changes in user risk.
  • Assure: Bank account verification, step-up authentication, qualified electronic signatures (QES), and Know Your Agent (KYA) to verify authorised activity and secure sensitive actions and transactions.

Shahid Hanif, CEO of Shufti, said: “As businesses expand, managing risk effectively requires more than adding new tools, technology, or collecting information. The real challenge is making critical data available when decisions need to be made, regardless of where it originates or which team holds it. With Shufti Glocal Trust OS, our vision is to give businesses greater consistency, clarity, and control over risk management and making informed decisions as their operations grow.”

Glocal by Design, Global Reach with Local Adaptability

While the Trust operating system connects business functions, its Glocal foundation allows businesses to address the regulatory and operational differences between markets.

Glocal Trust OS combines global technology with verification methods and risk controls adapted to local requirements. Businesses can also configure tailored workflows around their own policies, risk appetite, and operating procedures, maintaining a unified platform across jurisdictions without applying identical controls in every jurisdiction.

data.title: Exclusive-Canada's BMO returning to US oil and gas investment banking, sources say
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Bank of Montreal ( AIQD ) is reviving its investment banking service to oil and gas companies in the United States, six years after it exited, and is hiring bankers from Mizuho Financial Group as part of the push, people familiar with the matter said.

The bank's investment banking arm, BMO Capital Markets, is hiring Ali Akbar to run its rebuilt U.S. energy practice, said the sources, who declined to be named discussing private information.

Focused on midstream companies and other energy infrastructure operators, Akbar is a veteran dealmaker with more than 25 years of investment banking experience, most recently at Mizuho and its Greenhill unit, and prior to that at RBC Capital Markets and Deutsche Bank, according to an online profile.

BMO is also poaching other energy bankers from Mizuho, who will join under Akbar next year, following a standard period known in the industry as gardening leave, the sources said. The identities of the other bankers could not be learned.

BMO and Mizuho declined comment.

The return of BMO to US oil and gas investment banking comes at a time when the American energy sector finds itself in rude health, buoyed by natural gas' critical role in power generation to support the build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure, as well as the nation's stable operating environment away from conflict zones in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. 

This has supported dealmaking activity, with operators acquiring to boost growth, and foreign buyers and non-traditional investors drawn in by the opportunity.

BMO pulled out of oil and gas investment banking outside of Canada in late 2020, at the end of a year where the COVID-19 pandemic decimated energy demand, crude prices turned negative for the first time in history, and dozens of U.S. oil and gas companies were forced to file for bankruptcy. 

North America's energy market has shown signs of further interconnection in the last couple of years. Canadian pipeline companies continue to grow their substantial businesses south of the border, while U.S. energy producers are looking to Canada as prime shale sites in their home market dwindle.

(Reporting by David French in New York; editing by Echo Wang and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Goolsbee says the Fed's job right now is to keep AI surge from overheating the economy
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Artificial intelligence may lead to a productivity boom in the future, but the US Federal Reserve's job in the meantime is to keep inflation in check amid strong investment and demand, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday. 

"If you hand people a trillion dollars of wealth, they're going to spend it," Goolsbee said, speaking at an Indiana economic forum on the day AI firm Anthropic held its record-setting public stock offering. "Two forces, the building up of data centers ... and consumers spending out of future wealth, those can easily overheat the economy ... The Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy."

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Chris Reese)

data.title: Rapid AI Buildout Putting Upward Pressure on Inflation, Fed Vice Chair Jefferson Says
data.description:
01:39 PM EST, 11/19/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The ongoing artificial intelligence buildout is putting upward pressure on inflation, though productivity gains through technological advancements could help ease such pressures in the future, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said Thursday.

Adoption of AI by businesses has increased "considerably" over the last two years, Jefferson said in remarks prepared for delivery at a conference in Brazil.

The AI boom has driven investments in data centers and advanced computing equipment, with expectations for a boost to productivity and output, he said.

"Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation," Jefferson said. "In the future, advancements in productivity could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth."

Earlier in the week, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh underscored potential economic gains and losses from AI, saying the technology will have key implications for monetary policy. It could either drive sustained above-average economic growth or trigger layoffs amid an economic slowdown, depending on how the technology progresses, Warsh said at the time.

While AI could cause some job displacement, it could result in new jobs and firms that "we have not yet imagined," Jefferson said Thursday.

In a report last month, JPMorgan said Amazon.com (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), Oracle (ORCL) and Microsoft (MSFT) are expected to spend $900 billion on AI this year.

On Wednesday, minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed that almost all policymakers agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation. "Many participants viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk," according to the minutes.

Also on Wednesday, Fed Governor Michael Barr said raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the central bank's 2% target in a timely manner, joining other Fed officials who have recently leaned hawkish. US inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years.

Markets widely expect the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee to raise interest rate by 25 basis points next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

DENVER and CORK, Ireland, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Poppulo, the only Employee Experience Platform that transforms how leaders align, assure, and activate their people, today announced it has been recognized as a Visionary in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Frontline Worker Communication Applications. It is the first Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for the category, which covers software for the majority of the world’s workforce.

“For far too long, the people who keep factories, hospitals, stores, and supply chains running have had less access than their desk-based colleagues to the information and systems they need to do their jobs,” said Ruth Fornell, CEO, Poppulo. “We think a Magic Quadrant dedicated to frontline communication shows how far that has changed.”

“We believe our recognition as a Visionary in this critical category reflects the breadth of what we’ve built: one platform that reaches a nurse on a night shift or a technician on a site visit as easily as someone at a desk in head office,” said Fornell. “We give every employee an integrated, connected experience where they can find trusted information and act on it, wherever and however they work.”

Gartner assessed vendors in the Frontline Worker Communication Applications report on Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute. In October, Poppulo was also named a Challenger in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Intranet Packaged Solutions.

Manufacturers, healthcare providers, retailers, and logistics companies employ people who work across sites and shifts, often in several languages and with uneven access to devices. Communicators need to get consistent, relevant messages to all of them and help them find the procedures they need. They also need proof that the messages got through.

Poppulo is built for that job. It delivers messages through mobile, web, digital signage, and email from a single unified platform, so employees receive them whatever their access to devices. Audience targeting and centralized planning keep messages consistent and relevant to each site and shift, while delegated publishing lets local teams post their own updates. Engagement analytics provide the proof across digital and physical channels.

Among a growing set of AI capabilities, Poppulo’s Ask AI lets employees ask questions the way they would ask a colleague.

“AI is changing how employees access information and how communicators support them,” said Fornell. “With Ask AI, an employee can find a policy or procedure without knowing where it’s stored, and the answer comes from content the company has approved. Alongside that, we’re giving communications teams the tools to create and deliver content more efficiently, including video and audio dubbing with lip-sync to support multilingual communications.”

Poppulo’s acquisition of Sociabble in May 2026 expanded its platform, which now spans multichannel communications, intranet, knowledge management, employee engagement, and advocacy. Poppulo is among a select group of vendors included in both Magic Quadrants, and the company believes this reflects a platform built for frontline and desk-based employees alike, across the digital and physical workplace.

data.title: US was warned of telecom security risks years before Salt Typhoon
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government was warned in a report it commissioned about major national security risks from weaknesses in the country's telecom networks in 2022, two years before sweeping Chinese-linked cyberespionage known as Salt Typhoon.

The report commissioned by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said US telecommunications networks contained "major structural vulnerabilities" and could be compromised from anywhere in the world.

US officials have previously alleged that hackers targeted nine telecom companies, including Verizon, AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile and Lumen, during the 2024 Salt Typhoon campaign and stole telephone audio intercepts and a large tranche of call-record data.

The report, disclosed as part of a lawsuit, has been reviewed by Reuters.

Details of the report were first reported by Bloomberg News on Thursday.

The June 2022 report described US telecom infrastructure as one in a "perilous and untenable situation," and added that international interconnects could provide attackers with "trusted" access. "The fact that US national networks can be readily compromised from anywhere in the world is not yet widely understood."

CISA withheld the report from public release for four years and resisted congressional pressure to publish it, according to Bloomberg News.

The agency did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Ron Wyden, a Democratic senator from Oregon, pushed for the release of the report last year. He had said in a statement, "Congress would have had ample time to require mandatory cybersecurity standards for phone companies, in time to prevent the Salt Typhoon hacks" had the report been made public when it was first written.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

The letter, addressed to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, search head Elizabeth Reid and education vice president Chris Phillips, said that "cutting off access to Search for schools that don't wish to use AI will not help persuade our users," and would more likely lead them to shut out Google products altogether, according to the report. More than 540 Google employees and contractors signed the letter, Bloomberg said.

Google plans to turn off AI tools, including its search engine, by default for K-12 student accounts, Bloomberg reported. Schools that enable Google Search would have to accept its AI features.

Senator Ed Markey, a Massachusetts Democrat, has urged Google to change course, according to the report. Dan Carroll, co-founder of ed tech startup Clever, told Bloomberg that Google faces "a real strategic pickle" between offering schools an AI-free search that may feel outdated and alienating schools by requiring the new version.

data.title: Trump's defamation case against New York Times and Penguin Random House may proceed, judge rules
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - A federal judge on Thursday said President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the New York Times ( NYT ) and book publisher Penguin Random House may proceed, a victory for Trump in his legal campaign against media companies he accuses of treating him unfairly.

Trump has filed several lawsuits against media companies since 2024, alleging they defamed him or fraudulently misled the public with false coverage. His critics have denounced the lawsuits as attacks on the free press.

The lawsuit against the New York Times ( NYT ) and Penguin Random House cited a book about Trump by two New York Times reporters and what it characterized as "false, malicious, defamatory, and disparaging" articles that he says were aimed at sabotaging his chances in the 2024 presidential election, which he won.

The Times and Penguin have denied defaming Trump and said in a court filing that his case is legally flawed and aimed at scoring political points.

Representatives for the New York Times ( NYT ), Penguin Random House and Trump's personal lawyers did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

US District Judge Steven Merryday, an appointee of George H.W. Bush, handed down the ruling in federal court in Tampa, Florida.

Merryday threw out two of Trump's claims but said the rest of his complaint plausibly alleged that statements accusing Trump of "planning and perpetrating complex crimes" were "based on incomplete, minimal information."

The lawsuit against the Times and Penguin concerned two articles and a book that cast doubts on his origin story as a savvy businessman who ascended in the real estate and entertainment industries.

Trump cited 22 statements from the book by Times journalist Peter Baker titled "For Trump, a Lifetime of Scandals Heads Toward a Moment of Judgment" and 12 from the articles by Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner.

They include assertions about Trump's role in creating his hit reality TV show "The Apprentice," his inheritance from his father, his business ventures and upbringing in New York City.

The Times and Penguin said in a motion to dismiss that Trump's lawsuit failed to explain how the statements were defamatory and included subjective opinions that cannot be proven true or false.

(Reporting by Luc Cohen in New York; Editing by Noeleen Walder)

data.title: Parasail Adds Positron Titan to Cut Cost of Running Trillion-Parameter Models for AI Agents
data.description:
Customers will run the largest open-weight models on Titan through the same Parasail API, committing to output instead of hardware

SAN MATEO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Parasail, the first multi-silicon inference cloud, today announced it will deploy 5 megawatts of Positron AI's next-generation Titan inference systems. Parasail expects the Titan capacity, which comes online in late 2027, to serve trillions of tokens a day for companies building on frontier-scale open-weight models. The deal expands a partnership in which Positron’s first-generation Atlas systems already serve Parasail customers.

Titan runs multi-trillion-parameter models on low-power LPDDR5X, a commodity DRAM, in place of the high-bandwidth memory GPUs rely on. Compared to traditional GPUs, Titan delivers 2.4x the tokens per dollar, or, at the same cost per token, 4.1x the speed. Customers will reach Titan through the same Parasail account and OpenAI-compatible API they already use. Titan joins Parasail’s multi-silicon fleet that is already serving trillions of tokens a day.

“No single chip is best at every AI workload, so building an inference cloud around just one never made sense," said Mike Henry, co-founder and CEO of Parasail. “Positron fills a critical part of our fleet for token traffic that is highly sensitive to cost and needs titanic scale up. We see their Titan Systems being instrumental in long-running agents, agent swarms, and physical AI and robotics use cases that have to run in power constrained environments.”

“Agents need the largest models, and running the largest models is a memory problem,” said Mitesh Agrawal, CEO of Positron AI. “We built Titan to hold multi-trillion-parameter models in low-power commodity memory. Parasail already runs our Atlas systems in production, and it knows how to get new silicon to customers at scale.”

About Parasail

Parasail is the first multi-silicon AI inference cloud designed to intelligently route different AI workloads to the hardware best suited to run them. Combining intelligent orchestration with advanced kernel optimization, Parasail builds on its established GPU infrastructure to deliver high-performance, cost-efficient inference through a unified platform. As AI computing technology advances, Parasail is designed to incorporate those innovations so customers can benefit from ongoing improvements in performance and efficiency without managing multiple hardware providers or having to replatform. Parasail is headquartered in San Mateo, California, and backed by Kindred Ventures, Touring Capital, Basis Set, and others. Learn more at parasail.io.

About Positron AI

Positron AI builds hardware and software to make AI inference dramatically cheaper and more energy efficient. The company’s shipping product, Atlas, is deployed at hyperscaler scale today, and its next-generation custom silicon, Asimov, tapes out in late 2026 with production in the second half of 2027. Asimov powers Titan, a multi-terabyte-memory inference system for long-context and next-generation AI workloads. Positron’s energy-efficient architecture allows its systems to be deployed in air-cooled or liquid-cooled data centers at varying rack densities, without dependence on constrained HBM or CoWoS supply chains. Learn more at positron.ai.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Valkey 9.2 Lowers Cost of AI Workloads On Existing Infrastructure Alongside New Distributed KV Caching Capability
data.description:
The latest release targets three of the largest costs of running at scale: extra memory held in reserve for backups, cross-region network traffic, and memory overhead for large datasets.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Valkey, the open source datastore for high-performing systems, today announced the general availability of Valkey 9.2, a release built to help organizations do more with the infrastructure they already have. Version 9.2 is complemented by the launch of distributed KV caching, taking aim at inference costs by providing a large, shared cache across entire GPU fleets. Building on Valkey's core pillars of efficiency and performance, version 9.2 reinforces the project's commitment to scaling enterprise workloads while driving down infrastructure costs.

"A major ethos of Valkey is doing more with less, which means getting more functionality with less hardware."

Valkey sits on the hot path of modern applications, powering the caching, queues, and real-time data that users immediately experience. At that scale, every gigabyte of memory and every request sent between regions has associated costs for businesses, whether it's a part of historical operations or a new AI initiative. Valkey 9.2 continues the project's commitment to being efficient by design.

"A major ethos of Valkey is doing more with less, which means getting more functionality with less hardware," said Madelyn Olson, Valkey project maintainer and Principal Engineer for AWS in-memory databases. "We designed Valkey 9.2 around this principle to deliver reduced memory overhead, lower cross-region network costs, and worry-free performance. With each release, Valkey continues to prove its value as an exceptionally fast, efficient, and reliable datastore."             

Distributed KV Caching Maximizes GPU Servers and Minimizes Costs
Agentic AI applications waste expensive GPU compute by constantly reprocessing the same prompt instructions, tool definitions, and conversation history. Released alongside Valkey 9.2, open source distributed KV caching enhances AI workload efficiency by creating a large, shared cache across a GPU fleet, allowing inference engines to reuse computed work rather than recomputing. Builders running open-weight models on self-managed inference can now connect a distributed KV cache through LMCache, which plugs into engines like vLLM and SGLang using a single configuration change. Distributed KV caching achieves:

  • Lower AI inference spend: Reduces costs by up to 40% by allowing teams to serve more users on the GPUs they already have.
  • Improved latency: Decreases time-to-first-token by up to 80%.
  • Seamless deployment, no vendor-lock in: Works on any cloud or infrastructure with zero application code updates.

Path Hash Makes Finding AI Context More Efficient
While distributed KV caching saves expensive compute, efficiently locating that shared context has traditionally required engineering teams to build and maintain complex, custom lookup logic. Valkey 9.2 minimizes this burden with Path Hash, a new native data type that acts as a fast, lightweight index for AI caching. Path Hash is to built to:

  • Simplify lookups and architecture: With a single command users instantly find the longest matching prefix and exactly where its cached results are stored, keeping large AI data in GPU or host memory while Valkey serves as the fast, lightweight index.
  • Reduce engineering overhead: Custom routing logic for AI inference systems is replaced with a versatile, general-purpose building block to quickly find matches on any hierarchical data, extending beyond AI workloads.

Forkless Snapshots Are Backups Without the Memory Spike
Historically, taking database snapshots on busy systems caused massive memory spikes – sometimes doubling usage – forcing teams to over-provision and pay for idle memory just to handle backups. Valkey 9.2 prevents this costly penalty by introducing forkless snapshots, which save data using a background thread instead of a separate process. The feature supports:

  • A flat memory footprint: Snapshots eliminate the temporary memory spikes previously required to protect data and bring new replicas online.
  • Right-sized infrastructure costs and predictable performance: Operators size and pay for infrastructure based on real workloads rather than worst-case backup scenarios, ensuring consistent resource usage across the system.

Replication Compression Lowers Network Costs for Distributed Deployments
Valkey 9.2 also tackles expenses resulting from cross-regional data transfers by introducing continuous stream compression. Replication compression provides:

  • Decreased network and storage costs: Ongoing replication traffic is reduced by roughly 50% to 65% and backup file sizes shrink by up to 80% (using the built-in LZ4 option), directly lowering cloud transfer fees.
  • Faster recovery: New replicas synced about 35% faster, and ongoing replication traffic shrank by roughly 50% to 65%, at a cost of about 2% to 4% of a CPU core per replica.

Sorted-Set Configuration: Faster Rankings, Less Memory
Sorted sets power critical features like real-time rankings, gaming leaderboards, and priority queues, but their traditional structure consumes excess memory and slows down as datasets grow. Valkey 9.2 fixes this by rebuilding large sorted sets on a highly compact B+ tree architecture.

  • Significant performance and efficiency gains: Delivers up to 105% faster updates and 36-43% better memory efficiency for sets with millions of entries.

To see what else is included in Valkey 9.2 or upgrade to the latest version, visit valkey.io.

Supporting Quotes

"With representation on Valkey's Technical Steering Committee, Alibaba Cloud is committed to advancing Valkey through open collaboration. We are proud to have contributed Path Hash to Valkey 9.2, bringing native support for hierarchical data and expanding what developers can build with Valkey. Drawing on our Tair team's research and practical experience in KV cache for AI inference, we see significant opportunities for Valkey in AI infrastructure. We look forward to working with the community to help Valkey meet the evolving needs of AI workloads and deliver greater value to developers."
– Guoyun Zhu, Head of Tair R&D, Alibaba Cloud

"Valkey has consistently delivered improved availability, performance and efficiency with each release. Valkey 9.2 is no exception, with forkless saves, hot key detection and even more efficient sorted sets. Momento and AWS have worked closely, and in the open, to advance RDMA for Valkey. It's a great example of the open source ecosystem working! Valkey proves that true open source doesn't lock innovation behind enterprise-license paywalls."
– Khawaja Shams, CEO, Momento

"At Multiverse Computing, we help customers scale inference workloads with compressed models that cut cost and latency. We cut both even further and served more prompts on existing GPUs by adding distributed KV caching on Valkey. With Valkey, we processed 50% more requests on the same GPUs within our one-second target for median time to first token. We achieved a 23% reduction in our median time to first token at normal traffic, and a 95% reduction at peak traffic. We also contributed LMCache connector improvements to the open-source community for Valkey that make distributed KV-caching more resilient."
– Ennio Pastore, Director of AI Platform, Multiverse Computing

"KV cache objects are large and latency-sensitive, which is exactly where traditional networking falls short. With RDMA, Valkey can move multi-megabyte KV chunks directly into GPU-serving nodes with minimal CPU overhead. That makes it a strong shared backend for LMCache deployments where many inference engines need to reuse the same context. More fast, open storage options means users can match their cache tier to their infrastructure instead of the other way around."
– Yihua Cheng, CTO and Co-founder, Tensormesh

About Valkey
Valkey is the open source in-memory datastore built for the core workloads of modern applications: caching, session stores, message queues, leaderboards, and latency-sensitive data paths. Designed for operational simplicity and cost-optimized scale, Valkey consistently delivers low latency at high throughput, enabling teams to run critical data infrastructure at any scale, without vendor lock-in or licensing surprises.. Governed by the Linux Foundation, Valkey is backed by a rich ecosystem of contributors and industry participants, including Aiven, Alibaba Cloud, anynines, AWS, BetterDB, Bytedance, DigitalOcean, Ericsson, Google Cloud, Heroku, k0rdent, Momento, NetApp Instaclustr, Oracle, Percona, Tencent Cloud, and UpCloud.

Linux Foundation projects are critical to the world's infrastructure including Linux, Kubernetes, Node.js, ONAP, OpenChain, OpenSSF, OpenStack, PyTorch, RISC-V, SPDX, Zephyr, and more. The Linux Foundation is focused on leveraging best practices and addressing the needs of contributors, users, and solution providers to create sustainable models for open collaboration. * Anthropic's blockbuster IPO keeps traders jittery

* Investor worries over AI trade linger

* Oil prices rise on Hormuz attacks concern

By Rodrigo Campos and Marc Jones

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Global stocks fell on Thursday as US stock traders focused on Anthropic's IPO, while oil prices rose as lingering attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz grabbed market attention.

Investors have said that how the first major AI developer to go public trades in the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge broader sentiment towards AI.

The Claude developer's initial public offering was priced at $83 a share, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion before the stock rose as much as 39% to trade at $115.10 on its debut.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,011.97 points, or 2.02%, to 49,186.20, the S&P 500 fell 110.35 points, or 1.51%, to 7,213.28 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 351.21 points, or 1.44%, to 24,078.68.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 14.30 points, or 1.33%, to 1,060.26. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.88%, while emerging market stocks fell 20.34 points, or 1.37%, to 1,463.94. Japan's Nikkei rose 419.93 points, or 0.71%, to 59,444.21.

The dollar index was steady after its recent rally to 19-month highs lost momentum.

"Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run," Shaun Osborne, chief ​currency strategist at Scotiabank, said, pointing to a pickup in risk sentiment linked to Anthropic.

The index was little changed at 103.81, with the euro up 0.06% at $1.098.

OIL EDGES UP

In commodities, oil prices edged higher as renewed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz offset a growing view that the oil market will soon be back in surplus.

Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media that two oil tankers hit naval mines in the waterway and "exploded" on Thursday. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

US crude rose 1.24% to $84.29 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.83 per barrel, up 0.96% on the day.

Spot gold fell 1.34% to $3,672.67 an ounce and spot silver fell 1.74% to $44.24 an ounce. Copper declined 0.3% to $12,433.00 a ton.

data.title: Africa's Digital Progress Accelerates, but 64% Usage Gap Shows Next Challenge for Policymakers
data.description:
GSMA Digital Africa Index 2026 finds seven more countries joining the continent's leading group for digital development and enabling policy

CAPE TOWN, South Africa, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Africa is making measurable progress on digital development and enabling policy, but turning widespread mobile broadband coverage into meaningful digital participation remains a critical challenge, according to the GSMA's flagship Digital Africa Index 2026, launched today at the GSMA Digital Africa Summit Cape Town.

Mobile broadband networks now cover 92% of Africa's population, yet only 28% use mobile internet on their own devices, leaving a 64% usage gap. The cost of internet-enabled devices limited digital skills, and a lack of relevant local content and services remain significant barriers. While the usage gap is a global challenge, it is largest in Africa, making accelerating adoption particularly urgent.

The Index, drawing on data from 54 countries, also points to encouraging policy momentum. Ten African countries now combine stronger digital development with more enabling policy and regulation, up from three in 2024. Egypt, Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Seychelles and Tunisia have joined Kenya, Mauritius and South Africa in the Index's leading group.

Angela Wamola, Head of Africa, GSMA, said: "Africa has made real progress in expanding mobile broadband coverage. The challenge now is ensuring that more people can actually use it. With 64% of the population living within coverage but not using mobile internet, closing the usage gap requires us to tackle the barriers that continue to keep people offline.

"South Africa shows what targeted reform can achieve. Making smartphones more affordable, building digital skills and ensuring people have access to relevant, trusted digital services can help turn connectivity into meaningful economic and social participation."

Device affordability remains a key barrier. South Africa demonstrates how targeted policy reform can support adoption: after removing the 9% excise duty on smartphones priced below R2,500 in April 2025, monthly sales of entry-level smartphones increased by 80%, from around 250,000 in March 2025 to around 460,000 in February 2026. The GSMA is urging governments where duties or sales taxes still apply to entry-level smartphones to remove those charges.

The Index calls for coordinated action across five areas: affordable and reliable connectivity; public value from digital services; trust and accountability; inclusive digital service design; and secure, connected government systems.

data.title: Tecore Networks Pioneers Purpose-Built Jamming Alongside MAS-E Following FCC Authorization
data.description:
Correctional Agencies Gain a Jamming Option Engineered to Protect Emergency and Public Safety Communications

WASHINGTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) today adopted a Third Report and Order in GN Docket No. 13-111, authorizing radio frequency (RF) jamming in state and local correctional facilities for the first time and marking a major milestone in the fight against contraband cellphones.

Tecore Networks, the inventor of Managed Access System (MAS) technology and an FCC-certified Contraband Interdiction System (CIS) provider, highlighted that its U.S.-made unified platform offers three-in-one capabilities: Barrage Jamming, Intelligent Jamming (IntelliJAM™), and Managed Access (MAS-E). While standard barrage jamming is now an option under the newly authorized FCC framework, Tecore's IntelliJAM™ serves as a highly engineered, dedicated jamming option designed to meet these new regulations. Rather than displacing MAS-E, IntelliJAM™ gives agencies a distinct alternative that disrupts contraband signals while maintaining a clear separation from emergency and public safety communications.

Contraband wireless devices remain an urgent threat across corrections. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr has cited estimates that upwards of 500,000 inmates have access to contraband cellphones, with roughly 25,000 devices recovered each year from state and local facilities. Illicit phones fuel extortion, drug trafficking, witness intimidation, and coordinated violence inside and outside correctional walls.

The FCC's action expands the toolkit available to corrections leaders without mandating a one-size-fits-all approach. As Chairman Carr emphasized, "It won't compel any prison to use jamming, and jamming may not be the right solution in every single facility," while giving agencies another option where warranted.

"For more than three decades, Tecore has engineered the cellular networks that keep society connected, and since 2008, we have applied that same rigor to stopping contraband phones inside correctional facilities," said Bipin Noble, Vice President at Tecore Networks and Corporate Chair-Elect of the Corrections Technology Association. "With the FCC opening the door to jamming, agencies now have a dedicated jamming option in IntelliJAM™, built to the FCC's new rule while protecting emergency and public safety communications. No single technology fits every facility, and because we build both managed access and jamming solutions, we can help correctional leaders match the right capability to the mission."

IntelliJAM™: Purpose-Built Jamming by Design

IntelliJAM™ provides facility-focused RF jamming structured to align with the FCC's regulatory framework and protect surrounding communities and critical communications. The FCC's new rules require every jamming deployment to prevent overjamming, blocking contraband phones inside the facility without disrupting service for neighbors, businesses, or first responders outside it. Rather than relying on raw transmission power, IntelliJAM™ uses precision RF engineering to keep jamming contained to designated areas. Built on Tecore's cellular engineering heritage, it delivers dependable coverage while respecting operational boundaries.

Key capabilities include:

  • Emergency and Public Safety Communications Protected: Engineered to maintain designated emergency and public safety communications, protecting first responders and critical operations in and around the facility.

  • Overjamming Control: Keeps jamming inside the designated perimeter so nearby homes, businesses, and roadways keep reliable cellular service, avoiding the service disruptions that can drive down neighboring property values.

  • Coordinated Network. Fewer Components: Minimal architecture with carrier-grade radios reduces reliance on numerous standalone jamming units, simplifying deployment, maintenance, and ongoing system management. Fewer standalone units also means fewer portable jammers that could be stolen or fall into the wrong hands, a risk the FCC addressed directly in today's order.

  • Compatible with Existing Tecore Deployments: Designed to leverage existing Tecore infrastructure already deployed in correctional facilities, providing a pathway to add jamming capabilities without constructing an entirely separate network.

  • No Rip and Replace if Switching to MAS-E: In the event an agency chooses to transition from Jamming/IntelliJAM™ to MAS-E, no rip-and-replace is needed. Because the same underlying infrastructure supports our three-in-one capabilities, Jamming, Intelligent Jamming, and MAS-E, agencies can evolve their interdiction strategy seamlessly and avoid the cost of replacing infrastructure.

Decades of Cellular Engineering. More Options for Corrections.

Founded in 1991, Tecore Networks designs and manufactures cellular network infrastructure, including core networks, radio access systems, and software-defined radio technologies for commercial, government, and military applications.

Since 2008, Tecore has applied that expertise to cellular interdiction within correctional facilities, pioneering managed access technology and continuing to advance its capabilities through Managed Access Evolved (MAS-E), powered by the company's patented Intelligent Network Access Controller (iNAC).

Every correctional facility has distinct architecture, topography, surrounding carrier towers, and risk profiles. Tecore pairs site surveys, RF modeling, and disciplined deployment practices with a full spectrum of capabilities, including MAS-E, IntelliJAM™, Barrage Jamming, and advanced investigative intelligence, so agencies can deploy what fits each facility best as licensing and compliance steps are completed.

"Because we engineer cellular systems from the ground up, we understand how signals behave in real-world environments," Noble added. "Whether an agency starts with Barrage Jamming, deploys IntelliJAM™, or transitions to MAS-E on the same infrastructure, our focus is giving corrections leaders compliant, dependable tools that protect staff, inmates, and the public."

Tecore commends Chairman Carr, the FCC, state and correctional leaders, and advocates who have worked tirelessly to address contraband communications. Tecore stands ready to support correctional agencies and policymakers as they evaluate facility needs, follow FCC licensing and compliance requirements, and deploy effective interdiction solutions.

About Tecore Networks

Founded in 1991, Tecore Networks is a U.S.-based innovator, designer, and manufacturer of advanced cellular network infrastructure and wireless communications technology. The inventor of managed access technology for correctional facilities, Tecore offers a comprehensive portfolio of cellular interdiction solutions, including Managed Access Evolved (MAS-E), IntelliJAM™, Barrage Jamming, and advanced investigative intelligence, supported by its patented Intelligent Network Access Controller (iNAC). Tecore's technologies are designed and built in the United States.

data.title: Houston refinery restart tests Trump's push to boost US fuel output
data.description:
* Valero plans to restore 165,000 barrel-per-day capacity

* Analysts estimate acquisition and recommissioning costs could reach about $1 billion

* Restart likely needs at least a year

By Nicole Jao and Arathy Somasekhar

NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Restarting a shuttered refinery near Houston, Texas, will be a costly test of President Donald Trump's agenda to boost US fuel output as prices surge amid a global supply squeeze, with analysts estimating the total price tag could reach $1 billion.

Refiner Valero Energy ( VLO ) agreed to buy the century-old LyondellBasell refinery for $320.5 million in October and restore a portion of the facility, returning 165,000 barrels per day of processing capacity by end-2027. The transaction is set to close in the fourth quarter.

The deal is the first of several recently announced projects to add new capacity along the US Gulf Coast, among the top refining belts in the world. US refiners are bucking a global trend of plateauing capacity as margins surge due to wars in Iran and Ukraine and as Washington pushes to expand domestic fuel output.

The plan would reverse years of refinery closures in the United States and add about 1% to overall US refining capacity of 18 million bpd. It comes despite long-term forecasts for declining US gasoline demand because of increased electric vehicle adoption and improvements in vehicle efficiency.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has stressed the Trump administration's support for the refining sector, saying his department is "talking about reopening every refinery we can."

Even so, the restart will not ease current high fuel prices because the refinery will not start producing fuel for at least another year, said Energy Aspects analyst Raul Calzada.

Restarting idled facilities also comes with a unique set of challenges. US regulators cited health and environmental concerns when rejecting an attempt to restart the St. Croix refinery in the US Virgin Islands, which was shut in 2021 after a chemical release sickened residents.

Valero did not respond to questions about the estimated refinery restart cost or whether the company has received regulatory permission for the project. The company generated $7.3 billion in adjusted operating cash flow in the third quarter, versus $1.6 billion a year earlier.

HEFTY COSTS

Houston-based LyondellBasell shut the refinery in February 2025 due to high operating costs.

Recommissioning the 700-acre facility would cost up to $700 million, said TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman. With the $320.5 million acquisition price, the total lands at about $1 billion.

Skip York, chief energy strategist at Turner, Mason & Company, also estimated capital spending would fall between $600 million and $700 million, adding the refinery could take until mid-2028 to reach full processing capacity.

Still, new refinery builds are far more costly. America First Refining's proposed 168,000-bpd oil refinery at the Port of Brownsville in South Texas has an estimated $5 billion total investment value, according to IIR Energy.

Gabelman said the acquisition signals that Valero expects stronger average refining margins over time than it previously assumed. He estimated the facility could generate roughly $150 million in annual free cash flow in a normal margin environment, implying a 31% internal rate of return.

Valero has said it expects to initially restart light sweet crude processing, with the potential to later invest in high-complexity heavy sour crude processing.

The Trump administration last month announced plans to provide up to $150 million in Defense Production Act funding to expand domestic petroleum production, storage, and logistics at US refineries.

No DPA funds were awarded to Valero in relation to the LyondellBasell refinery purchase, a White House official said.

Roughly one-fifth of global refining capacity faces increasing closure risk as oil demand approaches a peak around 2032, according to consultancy Wood Mackenzie. However, large, complex Gulf Coast refineries remain among the most competitive assets globally.

ExxonMobil and Chevron are also looking to expand capacity or upgrade existing facilities, while Marathon Petroleum ( MPC ) said it plans to reinvest proceeds from the sale of two refineries in opportunities primarily along the Gulf Coast.

(Reporting by Nicole Jao in New York, Arathy Somasekhar in Houston; Editing by Liz Hampton and Nia Williams)

data.title: Anthropic blows past $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut, tops SpaceX's June listing
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's market value hit as high as $2.1 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, soaring past SpaceX's massive June launch as investors rushed to buy shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company.

The stock opened at $111.5, 34% higher than the IPO price of $83. It was last trading at $105.11.

The stellar debut caps a turbulent week for the AI sector marked by Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's exit and shifts Wall Street's spotlight on to its rival OpenAI as the industry's next major public listing.

Strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia ( NVDA ) gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut.

AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

Anthropic, too, has signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Dario Amodei told CNBC in an interview.

AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show. Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares.

Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet's Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic also joins the trillion-dollar club stacked with behemoths such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ).

The blockbuster deal is going to earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

BIG PAYDAY FOR CO-FOUNDERS

Although shares can be volatile in the days following a listing, Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires.

Based on the IPO price, CEO Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes valued at nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

More broadly, the listing is expected to create a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, CEOs and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"Anthropic is a one-trick pony. People compare it with Amazon because even Amazon lost money for several years, but Anthropic won't have that luxury," said Bill Gunderson, partner at GCG Advisory Partners.

"They've got to get to profitability soon."

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Editing by Christian Plumb and Arun Koyyur)

data.title: Fed's Jefferson says AI boosting inflation, productivity impact possible 'in the future'
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The rapid artificial intelligence buildout is putting upward pressure on US inflation through its impact on demand, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Thursday, with possible productivity gains that could help ease price pressures only coming "in the future."

In prepared remarks to a Brazilian central bank conference, Jefferson said the AI boom is the sort of shock that could influence both demand and supply, but at different points in time.

"On the demand side, optimism about the technology has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products," Jefferson said. "Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation."

Productivity improvements from the new technology could put downward pressure on prices, but only "in the future," Jefferson said, without estimating a timeline.

Jefferson's prepared remarks did not mention his current interest-rate outlook. The Fed is expected to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point from the current range of 3.75%-4.00% at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: TIMELINE-Anthropic's meteoric rise from AI startup to $2 trillion market debut
data.description:
(Adds debut trade in headline and paragraph 1)

By Manya Saini

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq at a $2 trillion valuation on Thursday after raising $81.3 billion in the world's largest IPO, making the Claude chatbot maker the first publicly traded frontier AI company.

The AI lab priced its shares above the marketed range, underscoring investor appetite for a technology that has attracted billions of dollars in investment and reshaped industries around the world.

Here is a look at the road to the blockbuster listing:

May 2021:

Anthropic, led by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, announces it has raised $124 million in a Series A funding round led by technology investor and Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn.

April 2022:

Anthropic raises $580 million in a Series B funding round.

March 2023:

The company releases a large language model, Claude, that competes directly with offerings from OpenAI.

May 2023:

Anthropic raises $450 million from investors, including Alphabet's Google and Spark Capital.

September 2023:

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) announces it will invest up to $4 billion in cash in Anthropic.

October 2023:

Alphabet's Google agrees to invest up to $2 billion in Anthropic.

March 2024:

Anthropic reveals a suite of AI models known as Claude 3. The company says the most capable in the family, Claude 3 Opus, outperforms rival models GPT-4 from OpenAI and Gemini 1.0 Ultra from Google on various benchmarks.

August 2024:

Anthropic is hit with a class-action lawsuit in California federal court by three authors who say it misused their books and hundreds of thousands of others to train its AI-powered chatbot Claude.

November 2024:

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) pumps another $4 billion into Anthropic.

March 2025:

Anthropic raises $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

September 2025:

Anthropic's valuation hits $183 billion after raising $13 billion in a new round.

September 2025:

Anthropic unveils the Claude 4.5 AI model, saying the newest version can code for longer uninterrupted stretches and handle finance and scientific tasks better.

February 2026:

The company raises $30 billion in a funding round, more than doubling the Claude chatbot maker's valuation to $380 billion.

February 2026:

US President Donald Trump says he is directing the government to stop work with Anthropic, while the Pentagon said it would declare the startup a supply-chain risk.

March 2026:

Anthropic files a lawsuit to block the Pentagon from placing it on a national security blacklist, escalating the AI lab's high-stakes battle with the US military over usage restrictions on its technology.

April 2026:

Anthropic debuts Mythos, its most advanced AI model to date, equipped with sophisticated capabilities and designed for defensive cybersecurity tasks. The AI startup also announces "Project ‌Glasswing," under which select organizations will be allowed to use the AI model to find vulnerabilities in operating systems, web browsers and other software.

May 2026:

Anthropic announces it has raised $65 billion at a valuation of $965 billion.

June 2026:

Anthropic confidentially files for a US IPO, edging ahead of rival OpenAI in a closely watched race to reach public markets.

July 2026:

A federal judge in San Francisco signs off on Anthropic's landmark $1.5 billion settlement of a class-action lawsuit brought by a group of authors who accused it of misusing their books to train its AI chatbot Claude.

August 2026:

Independent music publisher Round Hill Music sues Anthropic and Suno in California federal court, alleging the AI companies misused hundreds of its songs to ​train their systems.

August 2026:

Anthropic projects 2028 revenue of ‌roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, Reuters reports, citing sources.

August 2026:

Anthropic's annual revenue run rate topped $65 billion by the end of July, Reuters reports, citing a source.

October 2026:

Reuters reports, citing sources, that some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming IPO are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures.

October 2026:

Anthropic said it is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to balance broader public interests with profitability goals.

November 2026:

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64.4 billion in its US IPO after formally launching its roadshow.

November 2026:

Institutional investor interest in Anthropic's IPO outpaced the early days of SpaceX's roadshow, Reuters reports, citing sources.

November 2026:

Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market listing on record after upsizing its offering, valuing it at $1.5 trillion.

November 2026:

Anthropic hits $2 trillion in market value as its shares soar in their Nasdaq debut.

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru; Editing by Sriraj Kalluvila, Subhranshu Sahu, Shinjini Ganguli and Leroy Leo)

data.title: 2027 Hyundai ELANTRA and 2028 ELANTRA Hybrid Revealed at Los Angeles Auto Show
data.description:
• Eighth-generation 2027 Hyundai ELANTRA introduces bold Art of Steel design, advanced connectivity and safety technology, and expanded passenger space
  • 2028 Hyundai ELANTRA Hybrid targets up to 53 MPGi combined and introduces class-exclusive Stay Modeii for enhanced comfort and convenience when parked
  • Longer wheelbase provides generous interior room approaching mid-size dimensions and best-in-class rear passenger spaceiii including 39.1 inches of rear legroom
  • Pleos Connectiv, Hyundai's new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment and connectivity hub, combines a 12.9-inch Full HD display, Gleo AIv voice assistant and OTA updates
  • 2027 Hyundai ELANTRA and 2028 Hyundai ELANTRA Hybrid on-sale timing for the U.S. to be announced closer to launch

FOUNTAIN VALLEY, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyundai Motor America today unveiled the all-new 2027 ELANTRA and 2028 ELANTRA Hybrid at AutoMobility LA 2026 at the Los Angeles Auto Show. This debut marks the introduction of the next generation of one of the brand's most successful and longest-running nameplatesvi. Designed to stretch the appeal of ELANTRA beyond traditional compact sedan expectations, this all-new model pairs a bold and muscular look, closer to midsize-class passenger space, Pleos Connect infotainment, and enhanced safety features. Available with a choice of ICE or hybrid powertrains, this eighth-generation sedan isn't just more distinctive, it's more refined, connected, and capable than ever.

"For many customers, ELANTRA is their first experience with the Hyundai brand, and that makes this vehicle especially important to us," said José Muñoz, president and CEO of Hyundai Motor Company ( HYMLF ). "The all-new ELANTRA demonstrates that an attainable sedan does not have to compromise on design, technology or everyday usability. We want that first Hyundai experience to be one that builds trust and keeps customers with our brand for years to come."

"Customers have been very clear about what they want: great design, technology, safety and efficiency, all at a price that makes sense," said Randy Parker, president and CEO, Hyundai Motor North America. "The all-new ELANTRA delivers on that formula. It gives customers more of what they value while remaining an attainable entry point into the Hyundai brand, and that's exactly the kind of product we want to bring to the U.S. market."

Art of Steel Design Gives ELANTRA a Bolder Presence
The all-new 2027 Hyundai ELANTRA introduces Hyundai's Art of Steel design language to the compact sedan segment.

"There is an inherent beauty in a sedan because its proportions are honest, intuitive and functional," said SangYup Lee, executive vice president and head of Hyundai and Genesis Global Design Center. "With the all-new ELANTRA, we returned to that essence, then pushed it forward. Wide muscular fenders, a long hood and refined three-box proportions give ELANTRA a confident, athletic presence that challenges the conventions of the compact sedan."

New exterior colors further enhance the all-new ELANTRA's distinctive design. Graphene Green offers a contemporary character, Kodiak Blue draws inspiration from cobalt minerals, Quantum Metal provides a sophisticated metallic finish, and Volcanic Red brings a bold, expressive presence. The new ELANTRA is 188.8 inches long, 73.0 inches wide and 56.1 inches tall, with a 108.3-inch wheelbase. Compared with the previous-generation model, the new ELANTRA grows 3.4 inches in length, 1.2 inches in width, and 1.2 inches in wheelbase. Both ICE and hybrid models achieve a 0.26 coefficient of drag.

"In a market defined by affordability, the most radical thing you can do is put great effort into building a desirable car that people can afford," said Olabisi Boyle, senior vice president, product planning and mobility strategy, Hyundai Motor North America. "The all-new ELANTRA is that car: the design makes you want to look back at it after you park, it gives mid-size space in a compact sedan, and it has ICE and hybrid options to match what you choose to drive."

Midsize-Class Passenger Space in a Compact Sedan
Although ELANTRA remains firmly positioned within the compact sedan segment, Hyundai engineers expanded key dimensions to significantly increase passenger comfort and usability. Rear legroom increases to 39.1 inches, while rear headroom reaches 37.7 inches. Rear shoulder room expands to 56.5 inches, helping make the back seat more comfortable and more accommodating for everyday family use. The result is best-in-class rear-seat space, delivering passenger comfort approaching midsize-class levels without sacrificing maneuverability, parkability, or efficiency. Both ICE and hybrid models offer a spacious second-row seating experience that is suitable for adults as well as front- and rear-facing car seats alike. Slimmer front seat frames help create additional room for rear passengers without sacrificing structural strength. ELANTRA's wider cabin is complemented by second-row air vents, standard rear USB-C charging ports, and an available 60/40 split-folding rear seatback.

2027 Hyundai ELANTRA ICE Powertrain
The 2027 Hyundai ELANTRA is powered by a Smartstream 2.0-liter Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder engine producing an estimated 147 horsepower. The engine is paired with Hyundai's proven Intelligent Variable Transmission (IVT) with Shiftronic. The updated engine incorporates enhancements to thermal management, oil delivery, and ignition. The IVT also uses a wider ratio range and reduced internal friction to support efficient, quiet operation. Hyundai is targeting up to 35 MPG combined for ICE models equipped with 16-inch wheels. Final EPA-certified fuel economy ratings will be announced closer to the model line's U.S. on-sale date and may differ from preliminary estimates.

2028 Hyundai ELANTRA Hybrid: More Power and Greater Efficiency
The ELANTRA Hybrid features an advanced 1.6-liter four-cylinder hybrid powertrain paired with a six-speed dual-clutch transmission. Compared to the previous-generation ELANTRA Hybrid, combined system output increases from 139 to 155 horsepower, while targeted fuel economy reaches up to 53 combined MPG, positioning the new ELANTRA Hybrid among the most efficient vehicles in its class. The electric motor's output increases from 32 kW to 45 kW, helping raise combined system power with the help of an enlarged high-voltage battery (1.49 kWh vs. 1.32 kWh). Smart Regenerative Braking 3.0 works with steering-wheel paddles to enable driver-adjustable regenerative braking levels, including a maximum setting that can bring the vehicle to a complete stop, providing an EV-like one-pedal driving experience.

Stay Modevii Brings Hybrid Comfort to Time Spent Parked
The ELANTRA Hybrid's class-exclusive Stay Mode allows the vehicle's climate control, audio, lighting, charge ports, and select convenience functions to operate for up to 30 minutes by using energy stored in the high-voltage hybrid battery while the vehicle remains parked. Unlike conventional vehicles that typically require using the gasoline engine to idle to maintain cabin comfort, Stay Mode allows occupants to enjoy a quiet and relaxing environment without the engine running.

Whether waiting at an airport pickup area, taking a break during a road trip, or spending time in the vehicle while parked, Stay Mode helps maintain cabin comfort without requiring the engine. Once Stay Mode is activated, no additional user action is required to recharge the traction battery after use, as the hybrid system automatically manages battery charging during normal vehicle operation.

Pleos Connect Creates a More Connected Hyundai ELANTRA
The all-new ELANTRA introduces Hyundai's next-generation Pleos Connect infotainment and connectivity platform to the compact sedan segment. Built on Android Automotive OS, Pleos Connect delivers an advanced connected experience including a natural-language digital voice assistant and over-the-air (OTA) update capability, all while retaining dedicated physical controls for intuitive operation of frequently used functions.

Centered around a standard 12.9-inch Full HD display, Pleos Connect delivers a modern user experience that combines a smartphone-like user interface with vehicle-focused functionality and enhanced customizability. The platform supports cloud connectivity, wireless Apple CarPlay® and Android Auto™, Bluelink®, SiriusXM®, Wi-Fi capability, and access to Hyundai's growing app ecosystem.

The new ELANTRA is available with Gleo AI, an advanced digital voice assistant built on a large language model (LLM). This cloud-connected agent makes operating select vehicle controls and launching supported web queries in an intuitive and conversational manner. The system includes contextual language support, multi-command capability, and zone-specific recognition to enable use by drivers and passengers alike.

Over-the-air (OTA) updates allow software enhancements and feature improvements to be delivered without requiring a dealership visit, helping keep vehicle software up to date throughout the ownership experience. Developed around Hyundai's "Eyes on the Road, Hands on the Wheel" philosophy, frequently used functions including audio and climate controls remain accessible through physical buttons and knobs for intuitive operation and enhanced convenience.

Interior Comfort, Convenience and Connectivity
Designed to exceed traditional compact sedan expectations, the all-new ELANTRA's cabin delivers a more spacious, premium, and thoughtfully connected environment for drivers and passengers. Expanded interior dimensions, refined materials, and available upscale amenities create a more comfortable experience during daily commutes and longer journeys. Two standard front USB-C charging ports provide up to 100 watts of shared charging power, while a pair of standard 27-watt rear USB-C charging ports help keep second-row passengers connected. A separate front 27-watt USB-C data port provides additional connectivity. Available dual wireless phone chargers add further convenience for front-seat occupants.

Available features include Digital Key 2 Premium, dual-zone automatic climate control, heated and ventilated front seats, a power driver's seat with Integrated Memory System, ambient interior lighting, and a power moonroof. Together, these features elevate ELANTRA beyond traditional compact car expectations. For customers seeking a premium audio experience, ELANTRA is available with Audio by Bang & Olufsen® sound system with 12 speakers. Developed to provide richer sound reproduction and a more immersive listening experience, the system delivers exceptional audio quality for music, podcasts, and other media throughout the cabin.

Digital and convenience features include:

  • 9.9-inch Slim Information Display
  • Gleo AI digital voice assistant
  • Single or dual wireless device charging, depending on trim
  • Up to 100W shared charging through dual front USB-C ports, plus a dedicated 27W USB-C data port
  • Dual rear USB-C charging ports
  • Digital Key 2 Premium
  • Audio by Bang & Olufsen® premium sound system with 12 speakers
  • Bluelink® connected vehicle services
  • Over-the-air software updates

Feature availability varies by trim and equipment package.

A Quieter, More Refined Driving Experience
The all-new ELANTRA uses a stiffer body structure and expanded application of ultra-high-strength steel. Reinforced structural areas support improved collision performance while also helping create a more solid and refined driving experience. Additional noise-limited measures include an acoustic windshield, revised mirror-area sealing, enhanced carpeting, and updated suspension components. New damper and bushing technologies are designed to better absorb road impacts, reducing low-frequency road noise while maintaining vehicle composure through corners. ICE models employ a rear coupled torsion-beam rear axle, while ELANTRA Hybrid models feature a sophisticated multi-link independent rear suspension.

Hyundai SmartSense Safety and Driver Assistance
The 2027 ELANTRA and 2028 ELANTRA Hybrid offer a comprehensive suite of Hyundai SmartSense safety and driver-assistance technologies.

Features include:

2027 Hyundai ELANTRA U.S. Trim Availability

Key standard features include:
